summary: Frontend-only testing of new Move/Hand pan tool and Ctrl/Meta+wheel zoom in photoedit.in editor. All new features implemented and behave as spec'd on the happy path: wheel zoom in/out with ctrlKey and metaKey works; plain wheel does not zoom; zoom clamps at 25% and 200%; Move/Hand cursor is 'grab', Picker/Brush cursor is 'crosshair'; Move and Hand pan the canvas-stage by adjusting scrollLeft/scrollTop when pointer-dragging on the canvas element. Drawing tools still commit history normally when the user drags on the canvas. Tested via WheelEvent dispatch + real pointer drags on the deployed preview.

ui_bugs.issue: Pan pointer handlers (onPointerDown/Move/Up) are attached to the <canvas> element only. At moderate zoom (~120%) the canvas fills most of the stage and pan works fine, but at high zoom (150-200%) the canvas element visually escapes the stage viewport (see 'canvas offscreen' bug below), so there is no visible surface to drag on. In addition, the 'checkerboard' background area of the stage (the empty part of canvas-wrap and stage) does not receive pan events. User expectation is: 'I select Move/Hand and can drag anywhere in the stage to pan'. Recommend moving the pan pointer handlers to the .canvas-stage (or .canvas-wrap) element so pan works anywhere in the stage even when the canvas itself is offscreen or small.

Pre-existing rendering issue exposed by this feature: with the default sample image loaded, at zoom>=150% the <canvas> element's bounding rect moves outside the stage's client rect (measured left=-767, top=-1461 at 200% on 1920x1080). This is because .canvas-wrap has inline width:dims.w × height:dims.h (e.g. 1067x1600 for the sample image) while .canvas-wrap canvas CSS is hard-coded to 900x600, and the wrap is scaled with transform:scale() around its center. The canvas ends up in the top-left corner of a much larger wrap, and after scaling it is pushed offscreen. Visually the stage shows only the checkerboard with no image. This is not new to the pan feature but it makes the pan feature effectively unusable at the exact zoom levels where panning matters most.

action_items: Move Move/Hand pointer handlers from the <canvas> element to the .canvas-stage (or .canvas-wrap) so dragging anywhere inside the stage pans, matching common editor UX and fixing pan when the canvas is offscreen at high zoom.

Fix the canvas / canvas-wrap size mismatch: either set the <canvas> element's CSS width/height to dims.w/dims.h (so it always fills the wrap), or drop the fixed 900x600 CSS rule in App.css line '.canvas-wrap canvas{display:block;width:900px;height:600px}'. This will keep the image visible and pannable at high zoom.
Consider switching cursor to 'grabbing' during active drag by re-rendering (currently panRef.current mutation does not trigger re-render, so the cursor stays 'grab' during drag). Minor polish.
critical_code_review_comments: Editor.jsx is 966 lines, past the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into hooks (usePan, useWheelZoom, useCanvasTools) and sub-components (Topbar, Toolbar, RightPanel).
In useEffect wheel listener (line 80-92), the effect has empty deps [], which is correct since stageRef.current is captured at mount and the setZoom callback form is used. Good.

Cursor style relies on panRef.current inside the inline style prop, but panRef mutation does not cause re-render, so 'grabbing' cursor is never actually shown. Use a boolean state instead for the panning flag if the grabbing cursor is desired.

onPointerDown early-returns after setPointerCapture for Move/Hand tool; that's correct. But pointer handlers on <canvas> mean pan only triggers when the pointer starts on the canvas element itself — see high-priority bug above.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Wheel zoom (ctrlKey/metaKey), clamping (25-200), plain-wheel no-zoom, and cursor rules are all verified PASS via evaluate + dispatchEvent. Move/Hand pan verified PASS at ~120% zoom via real mouse.down/move/up on the canvas element. Pan verified FAIL when the pointer starts on the empty checkerboard part of the stage (not on the canvas element) and at 200% zoom where the canvas is offscreen. Root cause is that the pointer handlers are attached to <canvas> instead of .canvas-stage, combined with the pre-existing canvas/wrap CSS-size mismatch (App.css hard-codes canvas to 900x600 while wrap uses dims.w/dims.h).
